yearEndChecklist.title: Year-End Tax Settlement Checklist
yearEndChecklist.subtitle: Tax year {year} — tick off what you need to do, in order, from the 31 December deadline through the 15 January simplified service to submitting to your employer.

progress.title: Tax year {year} progress
progress.allDone: All done. Check the settlement on your February pay.
progress.saved: Your ticks are saved in this browser only.
progress.clearConfirm: Clear all ticked items? This can't be undone.

situations.title: My situation
situations.desc: Pick what applies and only the items you need are added to the list.

items.religious: I donate to a religious group
items.disabled: A family member has a disability
items.housing: Homeless household head with a housing subscription

dec.title: By 31 December {year}
dec.desc: Deductions count in the year you actually pay. Anything paid after the new year moves to next year.

jan.title: After the simplified service opens on 15 January {next}
jan.desc: Check and download your data in Hometax or Sontax under 'Year-end settlement simplified service'.
jan.basis: Dates follow the National Tax Service schedule from previous years (tax year 2025). The tax year {year} schedule may change once announced.

docs.title: Documents the simplified service won't show
docs.desc: Places with no duty to report may be missing. Get a receipt and hand it to your employer yourself.

submit.title: Submitting and settlement
submit.desc: Your employer sets the deadline. If you miss it, you can still claim through the May filing or a refund request.

pension.title: Top up your pension savings and IRP
pension.desc: Pension savings up to ₩6M, or ₩9M combined with an IRP, earn a tax credit (16.5% incl. local tax if total salary is ₩55M or less, 13.2% above). Only payments by 31 December count, so check your provider's cut-off time.

card.title: Check how you split card spending
card.desc: Only spending above 25% of total salary is deducted. If you're already past it, debit cards and cash receipts (30%) beat credit cards (15%) for the rest of the year.

medical.title: Time your medical payments
medical.desc: Medical costs count in the year you pay, and only above 3% of total salary. For a large bill, compare paying in December versus January.

donation.title: Make donations and political contributions
donation.desc: Only donations paid by 31 December count this year. Political contributions up to ₩100,000 are credited almost in full (100/110).

hometown.title: Make a hometown love donation
hometown.desc: Up to ₩100,000 comes back to you in tax and you get a thank-you gift. This year's credit covers donations by 31 December.

marriage.title: Register your marriage
marriage.desc: Register your marriage by 31 December 2026 and each spouse gets a ₩500,000 tax credit for that year (once in a lifetime, Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 92).

rentHome.title: Meet the rent credit conditions
rentHome.desc: You must be a homeless household head as of 31 December, with your resident registration at the lease address. Only total salary of ₩80M or less qualifies.

housing.title: Check subscription deposits and no-home certificate
housing.desc: Homeless household heads with total salary of ₩70M or less deduct 40% of housing subscription deposits up to ₩3M a year. Deposits by 31 December count, and you must give your bank a no-home certificate by the end of February next year.

dependents.title: Check dependent conditions
dependents.desc: Dependents need annual income of ₩1M or less (₩5M total salary if they only have wages), parents must be 60 or older and children 20 or younger. There is no age limit for people with disabilities.

dual.title: Split deductions between spouses
dual.desc: Each family member can be claimed by only one spouse. Compare which side gains more, and remember a working spouse's card spending can't be combined with yours.

child.title: Check the child tax credit
child.desc: The credit depends on how many children aged 8 or older you have and any birth or adoption this year. For dual-income couples, only the parent claiming the child gets it.

education.title: Check when tuition is paid
education.desc: Only tuition paid this year counts: ₩3M per preschool or school child and ₩9M per university student. From payments in 2026, arts and sports academies for 1st and 2nd graders count too.

download.title: View and download simplified data
download.desc: From 15 January, view it in Hometax or Sontax and download the PDF. If your employer uses bulk delivery, in previous years it went straight to them from 17 or 20 January.

consent.title: Get dependents' data-sharing consent
consent.desc: Adult dependents such as your spouse or parents must give 'dependent data-sharing consent' in Hometax or Sontax before their data shows on your screen.

fix.title: Re-check the final data
fix.desc: From 15 to 18 January hospitals and institutions may still be correcting data. In previous years, final data was available from 20 January. Report missing medical costs to the missing medical expense centre from 15 to 17 January.

missing.title: Find spending the service missed
missing.desc: The service only shows what institutions report. Compare it with the medical, education and donation costs you paid and get receipts for anything missing.

glasses.title: Glasses and contact lens receipts
glasses.desc: Optical shops don't have to report, so purchases may not show. Get a receipt for vision correction with the user's name (up to ₩500,000 per person a year).

uniform.title: School uniform and field trip receipts
uniform.desc: Middle and high school uniforms count up to ₩500,000 per child and field trips up to ₩300,000. If they're missing, get receipts from the shop or school.

academy.title: Academy fee payment certificates
academy.desc: Academies and sports facilities for preschoolers, and arts and sports academies for children under 9 or in 1st–2nd grade (from payments in 2026), don't have to report, so you may need a payment certificate from the academy.

religious.title: Religious donation receipts
religious.desc: Donations to churches, cathedrals, temples and other religious groups often don't show. Get a donation receipt with the group's ID number and the amount.

rentDocs.title: Rent documents
rentDocs.desc: Submit a copy of the lease, your resident registration certificate and proof of payment such as bank transfer receipts. The service only shows public rental housing and some card payments.

disabledCert.title: Disability certificate
disabledCert.desc: People registered under the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities and national merit recipients show in the service. Patients with serious illnesses needing constant treatment need a certificate from the hospital.

smeForm.title: SME employee tax reduction application
smeForm.desc: The 90% income tax reduction for young SME employees (up to ₩2M a year) only applies once you give your employer the application. If you haven't, submit it before settlement; if you missed it, you can file a refund request.

company.title: Check your employer's deadline and submit
company.desc: Deadlines vary by employer (usually mid-January to early February). Check the notice and hand in the simplified PDF with the documents above.

february.title: Check the settlement on February pay
february.desc: Your employer settles when paying February salary. If you owe more than ₩100,000, you can ask to split it over February to April pay.

missed.title: Claim deductions you missed
missed.desc: Add missed deductions in the May {next} income tax filing, or file a refund request within 5 years after the settlement tax due date (10 March of the following year).
